newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND'S BANK HANDLOWY CONVERTIBLE BONDS IN JUNE.
newsitem.headline: POLAND'S BANK HANDLOWY CONVERTIBLE BONDS IN JUNE.

text.p: The planned convertible bond issue of Poland's Bank Handlowy SA will take place before the bank's public offering planned for late June, a bank official said on Thursday.
Stefan Kawalec, Handlowy president's chief advisor, said that the issue with a par value of 112 million zlotys and paid for from 1996 profits, would precede the public offering.
The whole bond issue would be taken up by the state treasury, which would later sell it to help finance the social security reform.
"The (bond) issue will precede the public offering of the bank's shares, before the end of June," Kawalec said.
The treasury is due to offer 42.9 percent of the current Handlowy share capital in public subscription in equal institutional and retail tranches.
The bank is also seeking to sell another 42.9 percent of shares to a group of long-term international financial investors.

After the bond issue the public tranche, the institutional non-public tranche and the convertible bond issue would each represent 30 percent of Handlowy's capital with the rest evenly divided between the state treasury and the bank's employees.
Kawalec said the bonds would be redeemeable after 10 years at par value of 4 zlotys each or could be exchanged into one Handlowy share each 15 months after the issue date at the earliest.

Kawalec also only those who bought the bonds directly from the state treasury would be allowed to convert the bonds and any investor or a group of investors would be allowed to convert up to four percent of the issue in any given year.
He added the bonds would carry the same rights to dividends and new share issues as ordinary shares.
